title: RULES if the Parking Garage Has a Level That Isn't on the Sign #shorts
description_hook: You parked on level 3. The elevator opens on a level with no number, and your car is the only one there. A work of fiction.

lines.say: You parked on level 3. The elevator opens on a level with no number. Rule one: never ride it twice in a row.
lines.img: an underground concrete parking level at night under orange sodium lights, a single dark sedan parked alone between painted pillars, open steel elevator doors in the foreground

lines.say: Rule two. The stairwell has one extra floor going down. Don't take it.
lines.img: a narrow concrete stairwell descending into darkness, flickering wall lamp, metal handrail glistening with damp, one landing deeper than it should be

lines.text: IF YOUR CAR CHIRPS, DON'T ANSWER
lines.say: Rule three. If your car chirps, it wasn't your remote.
lines.img: close-up of a car's headlights blinking softly in an empty garage, wet puddle on the concrete reflecting the amber glow, deep shadows behind

lines.say: Rule four. Follow the floor arrows, never the signs.
lines.img: faded white arrows painted on a damp concrete floor curving between thick pillars, sodium light pooling on the ground, the far end lost in darkness

lines.text: WAIT FOR THE MACHINE TO SAY GOODNIGHT
lines.say: Rule five. Don't drive out until the ticket machine says goodnight.
lines.img: a lone ticket machine glowing beside a lowered exit barrier in an empty garage at night, soft hum of fluorescent light, puddles reflecting its screen

lines.say: When the barrier lifts, the sign says level 3. Where you parked.
lines.img: an exit barrier arm rising slowly in a dim concrete garage, headlights shining into a ramp that curves back down into orange-lit darkness

loop_back: The exit gate is on level 3, where you parked — so you are back at the start, before the elevator in rule one.

gumi.say: So. Which rule would you break first?
